name: OpenClaw
short: A personal AI assistant on your own computer that you message from your chat apps.
what: An open-source AI assistant that runs on your own computer. You talk to it through apps you already use, like WhatsApp, Slack, Telegram, Discord and iMessage, and it can take actions for you. You choose the AI model it uses.
who: People comfortable in a terminal who want their own assistant wired into their chat apps. The install is one line, but getting the most from it means setting up a model provider, channels and security.
needs: Node.js, which the installer sets up for you if needed. For a manual npm install: Node 24.16+ or 26.1+
An account with an AI model provider. OpenClaw itself has no paid tier, but you pay for the model you connect

steps.title: Finish the setup wizard
steps.text: On a fresh install the installer opens onboarding automatically. If you installed with npm instead, start it yourself:

try.label: From the README
try.text: Run openclaw dashboard to open the Control UI, then send it a message to confirm the assistant is working. Channel setup is at docs.openclaw.ai/start/getting-started

watch: By default, tools run on your actual machine for the main session. Read the security and sandboxing guides before connecting other people or exposing it to the internet.
Treat incoming messages as untrusted. Unknown senders have to be approved with `openclaw pairing approve <channel> <code>`.
The install pipes a script from the internet into your shell. That's common, but read it first if you're unsure.
